scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQ-FRAME.statement: Dispute surge is due to slow ticket response; AI agent will reduce volume.

H-AMI-READ-QUALITY.statement: Incomplete or delayed AMI reads cause estimation errors leading to incorrect bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced incorrect bill calculations.

H-FIELD-READ-DELAY.statement: Contracted manual meter reads are missed or delayed, causing estimate substitution and bill errors.

H-HANDOFF-LATENCY.statement: Nightly MDMS-to-billing export or daily field-read upload is delayed, causing stale reads in bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route completion for Aug‑Sep is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating that manual meter‑read collection fell short and may have led to estimation errors on bills.
Dispute ticket response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < 3 day SLA), indicating response speed is not the cause of the dispute surge.
Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 per month in June‑July to 1180 in August and 1260 in September, indicating a surge that began in August.
The observation shows that among disputed bills, more are based on actual reads (1785) than estimated reads (1240), indicating that estimation errors are not the primary driver of the dispute surge.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating that no tariff changes have been recorded in the billing system.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing delayed routes and estimated bills for affected customers. This suggests staffing shortages may be contributing to the dispute surge via estimation errors.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder asserts that no tariff changes have occurred this year, indicating tariff changes are not a contributing factor to the dispute surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes can be requested by the utility but must be executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation, aligning with the existing dispatch approval requirement.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows 320 accounts received estimated bills in the last billing cycle across 40 routes, indicating a volume of estimation activity.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows 14 lagging routes with low completion (sample 0.7), indicating delayed manual meter reads that can lead to estimated bills and potentially disputes.
